summary.headline: Audited as if it were a live shop, Shopify's Dawn demo store sells cleanly (10 of 10 add-to-cart tests worked, no errors on 15 pages) but gives conflicting delivery and return terms on its product pages, leads its home page with sold-out bags and shows no customer reviews.
strengths: Buying works: 10 of 10 add-to-cart clicks on 5 product pages, phone and desktop, added the right product and variant (clicktest/results.json)
No console errors, failed requests or broken images on any of the 15 pages rendered, and 74 of 75 links checked resolve (pages/*/desktop.json, links.json)

The first phone screen of the home page says what is sold ("Industrial design meets fashion.", "Atypical leather goods") with one "Shop now" button, and no pop-up interrupts any page (pages/home/phone-first.jpg)
Every one of the 32 products has 5 to 25 photos, and all 29 compare-at prices are above the selling price (shop/products.json)
Product pages load well on a throttled phone (lab LCP 2.2 s, no layout shift) and carry valid Product structured data; all 32 products are in the sitemap (psi/local-lab.json, shop/sitemap-urls.json)
Collection pages offer filters for availability, price and colour plus 9 sort options (pages/collections-bags/text.txt)
summary.read_first: This is Shopify's public Dawn theme demo store, not a real business: it was audited as if it were a live shop to show what this report looks like, so placeholder content (contact details, brand names, empty policy pages) is reported and tagged "Possibly on purpose". Start with "Fix these first", repeat each finding's "See it yourself" steps before acting, and use its "Fix with Claude" prompt once you have decided on the change.
summary.limits: Not covered: checkout and payment, emails after sign-up or an abandoned checkout, the Shopify admin, and what visitors in other countries see (the run's location is not recorded, so the cookie-banner point is to test). PageSpeed Insights hit its daily quota, so speed figures come from one local throttled lab run, with no real-user data.

qa.summary: Buying works: all 10 add-to-cart clicks (5 products, phone and desktop) put the right product and variant in the cart, and no page shows console errors, failed requests or broken images. The two faults found are small and both sit on policy pages: a cut-off size table on phone and a dead link in the returns text.
strengths: 10 of 10 add-to-cart clicks on 5 in-stock product pages (phone and desktop) reached the cart as the right product and variant (clicktest/results.json, verdict MATCH)
0 console errors, 0 failed requests and 0 broken images on all 15 rendered pages (pages/*/desktop.json)
66 of 67 internal links and all 8 checked external links resolve (links.json)
14 of 15 phone pages have no sideways scroll (horizontalOverflowPx 0) and the only fixed bar is the 65px header (pages/*/phone.json)

ux.summary: The store is easy to read: the home page says what it sells in the first screen ("Industrial design meets fashion.", "Atypical leather goods", one "Shop now" button), there are no pop-ups, and Add to cart worked on 5 of 5 products tested. The friction is small: sold-out items lead the home grid, and on phone Add to cart sits just below the first screen with no sticky bar.
strengths: Home first screen on phone shows a clear headline, sub-headline and one primary button, "Shop now" (pages/home/phone-first.jpg)
No pop-ups on any of the 15 pages on phone, and none after 12 seconds (INDEX.md overlays column, pages/home/phone-after-12s.jpg)
After Add to cart, a notification offers View cart, Check out and Continue shopping (clicktest/results.json)
Collection pages offer filters (Availability, Price, Color) and 9 sort options; the phone header has Bags, Shoes, Lookbook, search and cart (pages/collections-bags/text.txt)
Sold-out and unavailable variants are struck through, and sold-out products show a "Sold out" button instead of Add to cart (pages/products-small-convertible-flex-bag-cappuccino/phone-first.jpg)

design.summary: The theme is visually clean and consistent: one logo, one type family, and buttons, cards and headings that behave the same on home, collection, product and cart pages. The gaps are ones shoppers do not see directly: product-page gallery photos carry empty alt text, and non-product pages share the enlarged logo as their link preview. The demonstration notice on product pages and the placeholder brand are deliberate on Shopify's demo store and are not reported here.
strengths: Every one of the 32 products has between 5 and 25 photos (shop/products.json)
The home page has no sideways scroll on phone (pages/home/phone.json, horizontalOverflowPx 0)
Product and collection pages use their own photo as the link-sharing image (pages/products-helix-denim/desktop.json seo.ogImage)
Every image on the 15 pages has an alt attribute and none is broken; home and collection cards use the product name as alt (pages/*/desktop.json images)

copy.summary: The offer is clear on the home page ("Industrial design meets fashion.", "Atypical leather goods") and product descriptions are specific, but delivery and return terms disagree between product pages and the policy pages. Placeholder contact details and four brand names come from Dawn's demo content.
strengths: Product descriptions on the sampled bags state shape, material, contents and use, e.g. the Studio Bag fits "wallet, phone, 500ml water bottle, and sunglasses"
The home page sub-headline states what is sold: "Functional handbags made of luxurious materials" (pages/home/text.txt)
All 15 rendered pages declare lang="en" and the copy is in English throughout
Buttons say what happens next: "Add to cart", "Buy it now", "Sold out"

products.summary: The catalogue is small and tidy: 32 priced products with 5 to 25 photos each and compare-at prices that are always above the price. The gaps are housekeeping: a Sale collection that is not about sales, blank product types, and missing SKUs and barcodes.
strengths: Every product has at least 5 photos (min 5, max 25) and a description (shop/products.json)
29 of 266 variants carry a compare-at price and none is equal to or below the price, so the sale badge keeps its meaning (shop/products.json)
Prices run from 119 to 615 CAD with a median of 460, all in one currency (shop/catalogue-stats.json)

tech.summary: Technical basics are solid: canonicals on every sampled page, valid Product structured data on all 5 product pages, all 32 products in the sitemap and no third-party app scripts. The gaps are bare home and collection metadata and a 3.3 s lab LCP on the phone home page.
strengths: All 32 products from products.json appear in the sitemap (shop/sitemap-urls.json)
Product pages carry ProductGroup structured data with no invalid JSON-LD (ldInvalid 0)
Product page phone lab LCP is 2.2 s with CLS 0 and TBT 128 ms (psi/local-lab.json)
No third-party app scripts load (thirdPartyKB 0 in psi/local-lab.json; apps none in stack.json)

growth.summary: Shopify's own analytics is the only tracking found, with no ad pixels and no consent banner in the test location; on Shopify's demo store that is expected rather than a fault. On a live store the gaps would be ad and consent set-up and an email sign-up that gives no reason to join.
strengths: No console errors and no failed requests on any of the 15 pages (pages/*/desktop.json console and network)
Internal links carry no utm_ parameters, so real traffic sources are not overwritten (pages/*/desktop.json links)
Every page links to 5 social profiles in the footer and the menu (pages/home/text.txt lines 71-75)

trust.summary: Free shipping is stated in the header on every page, the About page tells a founder story with a quality promise, and the footer has an email sign-up. The gaps are policy pages that return 404 and are not linked from the footer, no reviews anywhere, and no back-in-stock option; much of this is deliberate demo content.
strengths: A "Free shipping available on all orders!" bar shows in the first screen on all 5 product pages checked
The About page names a founder, a start year (2015) and a "quality promise" (pages/pages-about/text.txt)
A Returns page states a 14-day window and the condition rules (pages/pages-returns/text.txt)
None of the 15 pages triggered a pop-up on phone (INDEX.md)

On the same page, read the "Free Shipping" block: "We offer free worldwide express shipping on all orders. You'll receive your order an estimated 1–4 days after shipment."

In the footer click "Shipping policy" (/pages/shipping): "Delivery takes between 2-4 business days depending on your location" and "Please allow 2 business days to receive your shipment notification email after placing your order."

The product page also says both "US domestic orders" and "free worldwide express shipping", while the store prices in CAD.
